description: Serverless packaging + deployment. Add the Vercel Python entrypoint (api/index.py exposing the Flask WSGI app), vercel.json (route all paths to the function + a daily cron on /cron/refresh + Python 3.11), a committed requirements.txt exported from project deps (Vercel Python uses pip; uv.lock is gitignored), an offline demo-seed so the deployed page is never empty with NO env vars set, a Makefile serve-vercel target, and a README DEPLOYMENT section (click-by-click Vercel + optional Upstash/Google env). Records that the SQLite-persistence/Render assumption is SUPERSEDED. DEPENDS ON FEAT-002 (the /cron/refresh route the cron hits and the snapshot-wired wsgi app) and benefits from FEAT-003/FEAT-004 deps being present so requirements.txt is complete. Ordered LAST.
steps: In vandy_food_radar/web/wsgi.py, make build_app() boot cleanly on Vercel with NO env vars: after building the app with create_app(config, repository=..., snapshot_store=...), ensure the offline demo path is populated so the page is never empty. Use a SQLite DB path from VFR_DB defaulting to an ephemeral path suitable for serverless (e.g. '/tmp/store.db' when VFR_DB unset) and, when the target day has no events, call seed_demo(repository=repository, config=config) once at build time (guard so a populated store is not reseeded). Keep `make demo`/`make web` behavior working locally (VFR_DB still honored).

Create api/index.py at the repo root: `from vandy_food_radar.web.wsgi import app` and expose module-level `app` (the WSGI callable the Vercel Python runtime serves). Keep it a thin re-export; no logic.

Create vercel.json at the repo root: configure the Python function for api/index.py, route ALL request paths to it (rewrites/routes so '/(.*)' -> the function), pin the Python runtime to 3.11 if supported by the runtime config, and add a `crons` array with one entry { path: '/cron/refresh', schedule: '0 11 * * *' } (once daily; 11:00 UTC ~ early morning US Central). Ensure static assets under vandy_food_radar/web/static are served through the app (Flask serves them) rather than requiring a separate static route.

Generate requirements.txt at the repo root via `uv export --no-dev --no-hashes -o requirements.txt` and COMMIT it (it must include flask, google-api-python-client, google-auth and their transitive deps; stdlib urllib is used for Upstash/Maps so no requests entry is required). Verify it is not gitignored (only *.db, .env, uv.lock are). Add a short comment/README note that requirements.txt is regenerated from uv when deps change.

In the Makefile add a `serve-vercel` target that runs the WSGI app the Vercel way locally, e.g. `uv run flask --app api.index run --host $(WEB_HOST) --port $(WEB_PORT)` (add it to .PHONY and the help table); keep the existing demo/web/run targets unchanged.

In README.md add a DEPLOYMENT section: (1) click-by-click Vercel steps — go to Vercel, Import the GitHub repo jingyu-ruan/vandy-food-radar, Vercel detects the Python function (api/index.py) and requirements.txt, Deploy, open the generated .vercel.app URL which works IMMEDIATELY in offline demo mode (seeded fixtures, in-memory snapshot); note the user performs the final click-to-deploy and that we do NOT authenticate to Vercel here. (2) OPTIONAL: create a free Upstash Redis database and set UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL + UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN in the Vercel project env to enable cross-session change-tracking. (3) OPTIONAL Google Calendar (GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CREDENTIALS_JSON, VFR_CALENDAR_ID, VFR_CALENDAR_WRITE_ENABLED, VFR_CALENDAR_PROVIDER=google) and Google Maps (GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY, VFR_MAPS_ENABLED, VFR_LOCATION_PROVIDER=google_maps) env vars. (4) Document the daily Vercel Cron hitting /cron/refresh. (5) Add an explicit note that the earlier SQLite-persistence + Render/APScheduler/gunicorn design is SUPERSEDED by this stateless-serverless + Upstash-snapshot architecture.
Confirm .gitignore still ignores *.db/.env/uv.lock and does NOT ignore requirements.txt, api/, or vercel.json; add nothing that would exclude the new deploy artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: `uv run python -c "import api.index as m; c=m.app.test_client(); r=c.get('/'); assert r.status_code==200 and b'Vandy Food Radar' in r.data"` succeeds with NO env vars set (offline demo mode; page not empty).
vercel.json exists, routes all paths to api/index.py, pins Python 3.11, and declares a daily cron on /cron/refresh.
requirements.txt exists, is committed (not gitignored), and includes flask + google-api-python-client + google-auth.
`make serve-vercel` starts the app locally and GET / returns the seeded page; `make demo` still works offline.
README has a DEPLOYMENT section with the Vercel import steps, optional Upstash + Google env vars, the /cron/refresh cron note, and an explicit SUPERSEDED-assumption note.
`make check` is green; the pre-existing 93 tests still pass.
verification: uv run python -c "import api.index as m; c=m.app.test_client(); r=c.get('/'); assert r.status_code==200 and b'Vandy Food Radar' in r.data; print('ok')"
findings: DONE. Files: (1) vandy_food_radar/web/wsgi.py — DEFAULT_DB_PATH now '/tmp/store.db' (Vercel fs is read-only except /tmp); build_app() reads VFR_DB (still honored by make web/demo), constructs SqliteRepository(db_path, check_same_thread=False), calls _seed_if_empty() which seeds seed_demo(repository, config, today=now) ONLY when get_events_for_day(target_date) is empty (guarded reseed), then wires build_snapshot_store(config) into create_app so /cron/refresh + change tracking are live. (2) api/index.py — thin `from vandy_food_radar.web.wsgi import app` re-export; the WSGI callable Vercel serves. (3) vercel.json — functions.'api/index.py'.runtime='python@3.11'; rewrites '/(.*)' -> '/api/index.py' (Flask serves its own /static); crons=[{path:'/cron/refresh', schedule:'0 11 * * *'}] (daily 11:00 UTC). (4) requirements.txt — generated via `uv export --no-dev --no-hashes -o requirements.txt`, COMMITTED; includes flask==3.1.3, google-api-python-client==2.200.0, google-auth==2.59.0 (+ transitive incl. requests pulled by google-api-core; our own code uses stdlib urllib). Contains an editable `-e .` line so Vercel/pip installs the vandy_food_radar package from the repo. Not gitignored. (5) Makefile — added serve-vercel target (`uv run flask --app api.index run --host $(WEB_HOST) --port $(WEB_PORT)`), added to .PHONY + help; demo/web/run/seed unchanged. (6) README.md — new ## Deployment section: click-by-click Vercel import of jingyu-ruan/vandy-food-radar (offline demo works immediately, user does final deploy, we never auth to Vercel), regenerate-requirements note, optional Upstash (UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL/TOKEN) with graceful all-NEW degradation, optional Google Calendar + Maps env vars, /cron/refresh daily cron note, and an explicit SUPERSEDED note (SQLite persistence + Render + APScheduler + gunicorn superseded by stateless-serverless + Upstash-snapshot + Vercel Cron); serve-vercel row added to tasks table. .gitignore confirmed: *.db/.env/uv.lock IGNORED; requirements.txt/api/vercel.json TRACKED. NECESSARY SHARED-CODE FIX (surfaced, minimal, backward-compatible): SqliteRepository.__init__ gained an optional keyword-only `check_same_thread: bool = True` (default preserves prior behavior for all existing callers/tests). Root cause: the single sqlite3 connection was created in build_app()'s thread while any real WSGI server (Flask dev server AND Vercel) dispatches GET / on worker threads, raising sqlite3.ProgrammingError (cross-thread) — this broke `make serve-vercel`/`make web` under a live server. Only wsgi.build_app() opts into check_same_thread=False. VERIFICATION: offline boot `import api.index; test_client().get('/')` -> 200 with 'Vandy Food Radar' (NO env vars); a real threaded werkzeug server GET / -> 200 with 6 seeded event-cards; `uv run mypy` clean (62 files); `make check` green; 138 tests pass (was 138 pre-step).
